questions.question: How can a process execute its critical section?
questions.solution_html:
• When one process is executing in its critical section, no other process is allowed to execute in its critical
  • section. Each process must request permission to enter its critical section. The section of code
  • implementing this request is the entry section, exit section and the remainder section.
questions.final_answer: implementing this request is the entry section, exit section and the remainder section

questions.question: What is internal fragmentation?
questions.solution_html:
• Internal fragmentation occurs when a fixed-sized memory block is allocated to a process, but the
  • process uses less memory than the allocated block, leaving the unused space wasted within that block.

questions.question: Differentiate Microkernels and Module based operating system structures.
questions.solution_html:
• Micro Kernel, contains a minimum number of functions that are required, data, and features
  • simply to implement OS. Features of Microkernel include Minimalist design. High flexibility
  • Reliable and Portable - ((3 marks))
  • Modular Kernel, is a type of kernel in which some parts of the system core will get allocated
  • in independent files called modules. This can be added to the system at run time. It usually
  • requires a small amount of time to load modules. Its features include
  • Monolithic design, Low flexibility, Efficient: and Performance-oriented. -- ((3 marks))
questions.final_answer: Monolithic design, Low flexibility, Efficient: and Performance-oriented. -- ()

questions.question: Compare and contrast paging and segmentation in detail .
questions.solution_html:
• Compare and contrast paging and segmentation in detail.
  • Paging is a memory management technique in which process address space is broken into blocks of
  • the same size called pages (size is power of 2, between 512 bytes and 8192 bytes). Similarly, main
  • memory is divided into small fixed-sized blocks of (physical) memory called frames and the size of a
  • frame is kept the same as that of a page to have optimum.
  • Segmentation is a memory-management scheme that supports this programmer view of
  • Memory.

  • Explanation of segmentation with Segmentation Hardware and diagram – (6 marks).

questions.question: How does shared pages help in memory management?
questions.solution_html:
• Shared pages help in memory management by allowing multiple processes to share
  • the same physical memory instead of keeping separate copies.
  •  Reduces memory usage: Common code (e.g., libraries) is stored once and shared.
  •  Improves efficiency: Saves space and allows faster process creation (e.g., shared
  • libraries)
  • (2X 5 =(10 marks))

questions.question: Discuss Dual Mode operation in operating system.
questions.solution_html:
• Dual mode operation is a mechanism that allows an operating system to protect system
  • resources by running programs in two different modes
  •  User Mode: Used for executing application programs. Has restricted access to
  • hardware and system resources. Cannot execute privileged instructions.
  •  Kernel Mode (Supervisor Mode): Used by the operating system.
  •  Mode Bit: A special hardware bit indicates the current mode (user = 0
  • Kernel = 1).Ensures the system knows which mode is active.
  • Explanation with figure give full marks.
questions.final_answer: Explanation with figure give full marks

questions.question: Write notes on Layered operating system structure.
questions.solution_html:
• A layered operating system structure divides the operating system into a hierarchy of
  • layers, where each layer performs a specific function and interacts only with its adjacent
  • layers.
  • Layer 0: Hardware
  • Layer 1: CPU scheduling & memory management
  • Layer 2: I/O management
  • Layer 3: File system
  • Top Layer: User interface applications
  • With suitable diagram and explanation of each layer -(5 marks).
questions.final_answer: With suitable diagram and explanation of each layer
